title: Money and treats
intro: Money talk. I won't open your bank app, promise.

cards.prompt: You find $200 in a jacket you haven't worn since last winter.

options.t: Concert tickets. Tonight if possible.
Straight into savings. Future me says thanks.
Dinner for my people. Found money gets shared.
It went to a bill. Romance is dead.

cards.mask: looks like a lucky find; measures whether spare money becomes an experience now or a cushion for later (L1)

friend.prompt: {name} finds $200 in an old jacket. Where does it go?

cards.prompt: At their housewarming, your friend says, 'I worked so hard for this.' Their parents covered the down payment.
cards.teenPrompt: Your friend's parents paid for a private coach all year. They made the team and say, 'I earned this spot.'

options.t: Fair. They did work hard, and it shows.
True. And the head start did a lot of lifting.

cards.mask: looks like a hot take on a friend; measures whether you credit effort or name the family head start (T15)

friend.prompt: A friend with parent-funded help says 'I worked so hard for this.' What does {name} think?

b.t: Sure, with a big head start.

cards.prompt: Two pairs of sneakers. Both comfy, both last for years, both in budget. One is the pair you love. It costs $80 more.

options.t: The pair I love. I'll smile every time I lace up.
The other pair. That $80 already has plans.

cards.mask: looks like a shopping choice; measures paying for what delights you versus keeping the difference (T14)

friend.prompt: {name} can afford either pair of sneakers. The favorite pair costs $80 more. Which one?

b.t: The cheaper pair that does the same job.

cards.prompt: A plant for your room. $10 at the big store, or $13 from a neighbor whose sales fund the local animal shelter.

options.t: The neighbor's. Three dollars for the shelter dogs.
The $10 one. I'll give to causes when I choose.

cards.mask: looks like a price check; measures paying extra so a purchase helps someone versus budget first (T23)

friend.prompt: {name} can buy a plant for $10, or for $13 from a neighbor raising money for the animal shelter. Which?

cards.prompt: Think of the last time you wanted something you already had plenty of. Clothes, sneakers, figures, skins, mugs. What did you do?

options.t: Bought it on the spot. A new look is half the fun.
Cleared out a few old ones first, then bought it.
Left it in my cart until the feeling passed.
Bought it, then hid the bag for a few days.
Money said no, so that was that.

cards.mask: looks like a shopping confession; measures whether a full collection limits a new treat (T14, did-grade)

friend.prompt: {name} already has plenty of sneakers and spots a new pair to love. What happens?

cards.prompt: Right after that, what showed up first?

options.t: A little jolt of joy.
A tiny 'did I really need that?'
Relief. Decision made, done.
Pride. I stuck to my plan.
Worry. I opened the bank app.

cards.mask: looks like a quick mood check; measures the emotion attached to treating yourself (emotion only)

cards.prompt: Your group of four runs a weekend pop-up and makes $400. Everyone put in the same hours. One person's idea sold most of it.

options.t: Bigger cut for the idea person. Results count.
Four equal piles. We all showed up.
Equal piles, then I quietly tip the idea person.
Put it to a vote. Whatever wins, wins.
Skip the split. Team dinner, all of it.

cards.mask: looks like splitting cash; measures crediting results versus shared effort (T15), with a fair-process exit (L3)

friend.prompt: {name}'s group of four made $400. One person's idea sold most of it. How does {name} split it?

a.t: Bigger cut for the idea person.

cards.prompt: Pick the two that are the most you.

options.t: I have a savings goal with a name.
I've booked something before checking my balance.
I own the fancy version of one boring thing.
I've bragged about a dupe for a full week.
I could tell you my balance right now.
My fun money is gone by the 10th. Somehow.

cards.mask: looks like a money meme list; measures save versus leap (L1, T13), treat versus trim (T14) and track versus feel (T24), each slight

cards.prompt: The bill lands at group dinner. You're the…

options.t: Calculator. Everyone pays for exactly what they ordered.
Quiet coverer. Pays the broke friend's share, says nothing.
Speed splitter. Total divided by heads, no debates.
'I got this one.' Next round is yours.
Venue picker. Chose the cheap spot so everyone could come.

cards.mask: looks like a group-chat archetype; measures splitting by what you ordered versus by what people can afford (T12)

friend.prompt: The bill lands at group dinner. Which one is {name}?

a.t: Calculator: everyone pays for exactly what they ordered.

b.t: Quiet coverer: pays the broke friend's share.

cards.prompt: A limited banner drops tonight. Your favorite character, 48 hours only. You have $30 of fun money this month.

options.t: Pull. All of it. Tonight.
Wait for the rerun. They always come back.
Skip it. That $30 already has a job.
Watch a friend pull and scream along for free.

cards.mask: looks like gacha FOMO; checks the L1 and T13 read (leap now versus hold), with T24 and T14 as side guesses

cards.prompt: Group trip: the cabin is $400 split four ways. One friend quietly tells you they're broke this month.
cards.teenPrompt: Group day out: $40 each for the escape room and food. One friend quietly tells you they can't afford it.

options.t: Split it four ways anyway. Fair is fair.
The ones with more cover more. No speech.
Find a cheaper plan so everyone's in.
Cover their share now. They pay me back later.
Can't cover anyone. I'm broke this month too.

cards.mask: looks like trip logistics; checks the T12 read (same amount versus same strain)
